The layout check reads the width of the text from the full lines of this first page, which holds no image. The text is 6 in wide. A figure whose width plus its gap is 6 in or more leaves no room for the text beside it, so it takes the document default of 3 in, or 40% when even 40% plus the gap is 6 in or more. ## Widths that fit with the gap

![Fig G2in.](plot.png){#fig-g2in .wrap-right width="2in" wrap-gap="2em"}

Marker fits starts the paragraph beside the figure at 2 in with a 2 em gap, which together are narrower than the text, so the figure keeps its width. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.

![Fig G70.](plot.png){#fig-g70 .wrap-left width="75%" wrap-gap="25%"}

Marker sum starts the paragraph beside the figure at 75% with a 25% gap. Both are percents, so the render prints a warning, and the figure takes the 3 in default. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.

## A gap too wide for 40%

![Fig GWide.](plot.png){#fig-gwide .wrap-right width="5in" wrap-gap="4in"}

Marker gap follows the figure at 5 in with a 4 in gap. Even 40% with that gap fills the text, so the figure keeps 40% and the gap. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.
